content.text:
Set up a Node.js project (`fs-watch-mac`) for macOS filesystem watching:

- **`fsevents@^2.3.3`** as an `optionalDependency` (it's Darwin-only, so this keeps installs from failing on other platforms — the same pattern chokidar uses).
- **`package.json`**: `"os": ["darwin"]` restriction, `bin` entry, `engines.node >=14`.
- **`index.js`**: exports `watch(path, onEvent)`, lazy-requiring `fsevents` so the module still loads cross-platform and only throws when actually invoked off-macOS.
- **`bin/cli.js`**: simple CLI wrapper (`npm start -- /path/to/watch`).
- **`README.md`** and **`.gitignore`**.

Verified the module loads and fails gracefully with a clear error when run on non-macOS (there's no `fsevents` binary here since we're on Linux). Actual FSEvents behavior can only be exercised on macOS hardware.

Set up a Node.js project (`fs-watch-mac`) for macOS filesystem watching:

- **`fsevents@^2.3.3`** as an `optionalDependency` (it's Darwin-only, so this keeps installs from failing on other platforms — the same pattern chokidar uses).
- **`package.json`**: `"os": ["darwin"]` restriction, `bin` entry, `engines.node >=14`.
- **`index.js`**: exports `watch(path, onEvent)`, lazy-requiring `fsevents` so the module still loads cross-platform and only throws when actually invoked off-macOS.
- **`bin/cli.js`**: simple CLI wrapper (`npm start -- /path/to/watch`).
- **`README.md`** and **`.gitignore`**.

Verified the module loads and fails gracefully with a clear error when run on non-macOS (there's no `fsevents` binary here since we're on Linux). Actual FSEvents behavior can only be exercised on macOS hardware.
